newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescued yachtsmen get heroes' welcome.
newsitem.headline: Rescued yachtsmen get heroes' welcome.

text.p: Rescued solo round-the-world yatchtsmen Tony Bullimore and Thierry Dubois arrived back on warm, dry land on Monday to a heroes' welcome.

"Stepping off on to the shores of Australia has got to be the most exciting thing that has ever happened to me in my life under the circumstances," Bullimore said as after he walked down the gangplank of the Australian navy frigate HMAS Adelaide.

The Adelaide, which rescued the pair from freezing seas 1,400 miles south-west of Perth on Thursday, was greeted by flotilla of small craft and about 5,000 well-wishers as it steamed into the Western Australian port of Fremantle.
Wellwishers waved British flags and sang along to the tune of Waltzing Matilda on a sunny morning.
Many people held up banners saying "Welcome Home Heroes".
Family members were ushered on board the frigate to greet the two yachtsmen privately.
The pair were expected hold a news conference after on official welcome from Australian Defence minister Ian McLachlan.
Bullimore and Dubois, wearing grey naval uniforms with the name tags "Hon. 1" and "Hon. 2" emerged from the ship arm-in-arm to a loud roar from the crowed.
A smiling Bullimore was wearing a cap bearing the logo of an Australian TV channel which carried a live broadcast of the yachtmen's arrival.
The survival story of the 56-year-old former Royal Marine is expected to attract huge commercial interest from newspapers, television and movie studios.
Bullimore was rescued after surviving for four days in a dark air pocket in his upturned yacht, battered by Antarctic seas.
Dubois, a competitor in the same Vendee Globe Challenge as Bullimore, was plucked by helicopter from a tiny life-raft dropped earlier by the Australian air force.
